raw_comment:
I notice that the euthanization rate of cats and dogs from Dallas Animal Service has declined. The number of animals transferred to rescue or returned to their owner has also decreased. Another thing I noticed, was that while the decrease in euthanization occurred at a pretty constant rate, the rate of adoption was not so constant, as can be observed by the varying slope of the line. 

I wonder why the rate of adoption varies so much in comparison to the steady rate of euthanization? What factors determine the rates of euthanization and adoption? Are the factors the same? 

Catchy headline: Lucky Dog: A Look at Outcomes for Dallas Shelter Animals

raw_comment:
Thanks to all students who responded.  Great catchy headlines that capture the main ideas of the graph:  "The Struggle of Shelters is Shrinking Swiftly" by Team Wendy of Eden Prairie High School, Minnesota, "Things are looking up for homeless animals" by Abby, Maddix, Alex, Grace of Mason, Ohio, and “Saving a life of a shelter animal: paths away from euthanasia” by Ahona of Newton, Massachusetts. 

You can continue to post responses.  Please check back tomorrow (Thursday afternoon, October 24) to see the Reveal with a link to the original New York Times article, some questions about the graphs, and a few Stat Nuggets.
 
The next graph will be released tomorrow -- THURSDAY, OCTOBER 24, with moderation on WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 31.  You may respond before, during, or after the live moderation by going to “What’s Going On In This Graph?”  The topic --  ticket sales by sport.  Also, you can view the webinar with teachers and students discussing how to learn from graphs using The New York Times.  Go tohttps://webinars.on24.com/nyt/Graphs?partnerref=OnDemand.
 
Signing off – Sharon Hessney of Boston, who is thankful that the euthanasia rate is declining, and Chris Adkisson of Somerset, Kentucky, who can’t wait to give his dog a big hug tonight.

raw_comment:
Headline: Adopt from Dallas Today

I notice that the number of cats and dogs has decreased since 2009. In 2009, about 30,000 pets were euthanized but only 10,000 were euthanized in 2017. I also noticed that more people are adopting pets now. Other aspects that are notable could be the increase of released animals starting from 2014 and the spike and fall of transferring animals to rescue from 2017 to 2018. Animals are still being euthanized throughout the world still, just not as much.

I wonder why more people are adopting pets now than in 2009? What are the reasons that could cause a pet to be euthanized? What happens to the bodies of the pets after they are euthanized? Why did adoption rates go down in 2016?

raw_comment: First and foremost, we notice a steady decline in euthanization throughout the past few years. This is due to an increase in pet safety laws and PETA's growing influence. Overall, the downward trend is due to a decrease in animals going to this Dallas shelter. This can be attributed to movies like A Dog's Purpose and the cost of pet food. The sudden increase of pets in 2017 is due to Hurricane Harvey. The hurricane did not hit Dallas, and so, animals from shelters in the area that was hit were transferred to other shelters around the country (and even more so through the state). As a result, people were moved to adopt more sad, poor animals homeless by the hurricane. We wonder why there was an increase in animals who were released and what that means. We also are curious to know what this graph would look like today. Would there be an increase in adoptions? Would there be a decrease in animals arriving to the shelter? We love the title from Mrs. Lane from ELP Teacher: "It's Raining Cats and Dogs"

raw_comment:
Delta group,
We noticed a steady decrease in all categories up until the year 2016, where everything but adoption rates and returning rates to owners decreased, and the aforementioned categories rose with the rise in populations entering the Dallas animal services. Other things that are notable could be the increase of released animals starting from 2014 and the spike and fall of transferring animals to rescue from 2017 to 2018. We wonder if these things could be affected by weather outbreaks and modern social influences. Outbreaks of tornadoes and hurricanes could affect the population levels entering into the Dallas animal services because of the destruction of houses. The destruction brought with these natural disasters could misplace thousands of animals from their homes. The loss of their owner's life during these events could also be attributed to this as well. This could explain the spike in population as well as the rise in the returning rate. Modern entertainment, such as movies could affect this as well, such as the release of the movie "A Dog's Purpose" in 2016. Movies similar to the previous one could influence the viewers to make the decision to adopt as well as influence society to be open to rescuing animals.

Welcome to Wednesday's moderation of  “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graph shows the outcomes for Dallas shelter dogs and cats for the period 2009 to 2018.  

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?",  "What do you wonder?", and  "What's going on in this graph?"  

Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas about the graph. 

On Thursday afternoon, we’ll reveal the article that included this graph and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

The next “What’s Going On in This Graph?” will be released tomorrow -- Thursday, October 24 with moderation on Wednesday, October 31.  The topic – sports ticket sales.

raw_comment: This graph presents data related to the amount of animals euthanized (in the blue), and the amount of animals kept alive, either adopted, returned to owner, transferred to rescue in the red. From 2009 to 2017, there was an overall decrease of both animals euthanized and animals kept alive with alternative methods. This graph my be displaying the statistics of what is done to animals when they come into the shelter. It appears that prior to 2013, the shelter put more animals to death  through euthanasia rather than keeping them alive and actually rescuing them. raw_comment:
Adopt, Don't Shop!
Every animal my family has ever owned has been adopted. When I was 11, we went to adopt a kitten because we wanted a new cat. When we got there we found this old cat who had been there for over a YEAR and no one wanted her. We decided to take her and she changed our lives. Over the years since 2009, I think people have realized what a difference it is to adopt. This number has been decreased by 20,000 animals being euthanized over the past 10 years. I think that soon all Animal Shelters will be "No-Kill" and every animal will have a shot at a new life.
